newsitem.title: USA: Bodies of inmates feared switched in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Bodies of inmates feared switched in U.S..

text.p: The badly burned bodies of two inmates who died in a prison van fire may have been mistakenly switched and buried by the wrong families, their lawyers said Friday.

The wife of prisoner John Cannon exhumed what she was told was his body earlier this week after she read an autopsy report indicating the body had poor dental work. Tina Cannon told her lawyer Tim Maloney that her husband had good teeth.

Cannon was one of six inmates who died April 3 when the prison van in which they were shackled as it drove across Tennessee caught fire on a highway near Dickson. One of two guards was burned trying to open the rear door of the van, which was partially melted by the intense heat.
Frank Catalano, the father of another inmate who died, said he was considering exhuming the body he buried because the height and dental records did not match his son's.
Maloney said the inmates' two bodies may have been switched by the local coroner.
Tennessee authorities were not available for comment.
